result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.is_weakly_connected()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check if the graph is weakly connected. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L21550-L21615){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.is_weakly_connected() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} A directed graph is weakly connected if the underlying undirected graph (ignoring edge directions) is connected. Equivalently, there is a path between every pair of nodes when edge directions are ignored. For undirected graphs, this is equivalent to checking regular connectivity (same as `is_connected()`). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if the graph is weakly connected, `False` otherwise. Empty graphs are considered weakly connected (vacuously true). ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Time complexity: `O(V + E)` using BFS/DFS traversal. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Even though both edges point toward `B` (so `A` can't reach `C` directly), the graph is still weakly connected because ignoring direction links everything together: ::: {#3f544dc7 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("C", "B") # All connected when ignoring direction ) # Returns True graph.is_weakly_connected() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` True ``` ::: ::: ::: {#1aa1c565 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Returns False (can't reach C from A while respecting edge direction) graph.is_strongly_connected() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` False ``` ::: ::: Two completely separate components fail weak connectivity too, since ignoring direction doesn't create edges that don't exist: ::: {#515b4415 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="X") .add_node(label="Y") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("X", "Y") ) # Returns False graph.is_weakly_connected() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` False ``` ::: :::
